studies.Reference: Serum levels of dehydroepiandrosterone and its sulfate and the risk of developing bladder cancer.
studies.Title: Serum levels of dehydroepiandrosterone and its sulfate and the risk of developing bladder cancer.
studies.Authors: Gordon GB, Helzlsouer KJ, Comstock GW
studies.Timing: Serum donated in 1974 with subsequent bladder cancer diagnoses
studies.Population: Volunteers who donated serum to a community-based serum bank
studies.comparison_type: Decreasing prediagnostic serum dehydroepiandrosterone levels (cases versus matched controls), adjusted for smoking

sample_size.excerpt: We measured serum levels of both of these steroids in 35 individuals who donated serum to a community-based serum bank in 1974 and who subsequently developed bladder cancer and in 69 matched controls from the same cohort of volunteers. Prediagnostic serum levels of dehydroepiandrosterone and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate were significantly lower among cases compared with controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 35 + 69 = 104

cases.excerpt: We measured serum levels of both of these steroids in 35 individuals who donated serum to a community-based serum bank in 1974 and who subsequently developed bladder cancer and in 69 matched controls from the same cohort of volunteers.

comparison.excerpt: The risk of developing bladder cancer increased monotonically with decreasing serum levels of both steroids.
